facts.fact_text: A demonstration was planned to be held on 31 July 2010 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 2 April 2011 in Baku.
A demonstration was planned to be held on 17 April 2011 in Baku.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations in the centre of Baku, notwithstanding the Baku City Executive Authority's refusals to authorise the proposed locations.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicants, the demonstrations were conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding free and fair elections in Azerbaijan.
The participants in the demonstrations were demanding democratic reforms in Azerbaijan.
Participants in the demonstration of 17 April 2011 were also protesting against impediments to freedom of assembly.
Each applicant attended one of the demonstrations (as specified in the appendix).
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 31 July 2010 at the places indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 at the places indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 17 April 2011 at the places indicated by the organisers.

For both the 2 April 2011 and 17 April 2011 demonstrations, the Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) proposed a different location on the outskirts of Baku, namely the yard of a driving school situated in the 20th residential area of the Sabail District.
The organisers decided to hold the demonstrations in the centre of Baku, notwithstanding the Baku City Executive Authority's refusals to authorise the proposed locations.
Shortly after the demonstrations had begun, the police started to disperse them.
According to the official records, all the applicants were arrested during the dispersal operations.
According to the official records, all the applicants were taken to various police stations following their arrests.
On the day of the applicants' arrests, administrative offence reports (inzibati xəta haqqında protokol) were issued in respect of each of the applicants.

The administrative offence reports stated that by deliberately failing to comply with lawful police orders, the applicants had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
The respective first-instance courts found that the applicants had failed to stop participating in unauthorised demonstrations.
The respective first-instance courts convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).
The respective first-instance courts sentenced the applicants to periods of administrative detention ranging from seven to fifteen days, as specified in the Appendix.

The respective first-instance courts convicted the applicants under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (the CAO).

At the time of the applicants' arrests, Article 410.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings shall be given an opportunity to familiarise themselves with the administrative offence report.

At the time of the applicants' arrests, Article 410.4 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that an individual who is subject to administrative offence proceedings has the right to a copy of the administrative offence report.

At the time of the applicants' arrests, Article 437.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that a copy of a decision delivered on the basis of an appeal or a protest against a decision in an administrative offence case shall be given to the individual with respect to whom the decision was adopted within three days of its adoption.

At the time of the applicants' arrests, Article 437.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 provided that a copy of a decision delivered on the basis of an appeal or a protest against a decision sentencing an individual to administrative detention shall be given to that individual on the day of its adoption.

Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, paragraphs 27-42, 15 October 2015).

The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the other places proposed by the organisers for the 31 July 2010 demonstration were areas with heavy traffic.
The Baku City Executive Authority (the BCEA) noted that the places proposed by the organisers for the 2 April 2011 and 17 April 2011 demonstrations were areas with heavy traffic.

On various dates, the applicants lodged appeals before the Baku Court of Appeal, arguing that their convictions were in violation of their rights because the demonstrations in which they had participated or attempted to participate had been peaceful.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that their arrests had been unlawful.
The applicants complained before the Baku Court of Appeal that the hearings before the respective first-instance courts had not been fair.
The applicants asked the Baku Court of Appeal to quash the first-instance courts' decisions in their respective cases.
On various dates, the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' appeals and upheld the decisions of the respective first-instance courts, as specified in the appendix.
